name: Ensembling with pair_id-grouped cross-validation, probability calibration and NEGATIVE_OTHER threshold tuning
links: Grouped / stratified-grouped K-fold: scikit-learn GroupKFold and StratifiedGroupKFold (https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) ; fine-tuning seed variance: Dodge et al. 2020 (arXiv:2002.06305), Mosbach et al. 2021 (arXiv:2006.04884) ; deep ensembles: Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017 (arXiv:1612.01474) ; temperature scaling: Guo et al. 2017 (arXiv:1706.04599) ; F1-optimal thresholding: Lipton et al. 2014 (arXiv:1402.1892) ; weight averaging alternative: Model Soups (Wortsman et al. 2022, arXiv:2203.05482) ; task scorer and split policy: https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/ (evaluation_functions/). In-repo anchors: src/labels.py (REVERSE_PERM, reverse_instance_id), src/pipelines/eval.py.
license_access: Method only; open tooling (scikit-learn BSD, PyTorch). Inherits licenses of the ensembled models.
track_coverage: All four tracks. Groups must be defined on pair_id globally across tracks, because the same pair_id appears in T1-T4 (3 monolingual views + 12 mixed views per source pair); a fold assignment computed once and reused for every track and for any multilingual joint model prevents cross-track leakage.
basque_quality: Not applicable to the method; it inherits Basque competence from members. Ensembling is most valuable where individual members are weakest and noisiest (typically T3 EU), and heterogeneous ensembles (e.g. XLM-R-large + a Basque monolingual encoder) can combine multilingual alignment with Basque lexical coverage [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Ensembling reduces variance but not systematic cross-lingual bias; combining it with cross-lingual view pooling (averaging calibrated log-probs over all views of a pair_id) is the robustness lever. Calibrate per track (or per language combination in T4) because mixed-language inputs are typically less confident.
architecture: Protocol: (1) Merge train+dev (T1: 1,282 + 277 = 1,559 reversible source pairs, 478 + 106 = 584 NEG singletons) and build K=5 (or 10) StratifiedGroupKFold splits with groups = pair_id and strata = source label (EQ / FE-or-BE in canonical orientation / NEG); keep the official dev split as an extra sanity holdout once. (2) Train each candidate (backbone x seed x recipe) per fold; collect out-of-fold (OOF) 4-way probabilities for every row. (3) Calibrate on OOF: per-model temperature T (or vector scaling with 4 biases) fitted by NLL; symmetrise with the twin, p_sym(x) = 0.5*(p(x) + p(x_rev)[REVERSE_PERM]) in log space. (4) Ensemble: weighted average of calibrated log-probs; weights by OOF NLL or greedy forward selection (Caruana) on the official metric; optionally stack with logistic regression on OOF. (5) Decision: joint pair decoding over consistent label pairs plus a NEG decision rule tuned on OOF: predict NEG if p_NEG (pair-averaged) > tau, or add a bias b to the NEG logit; choose tau/b to maximise Weighted F1 (and check HardCons) on OOF, not on the 383-group dev set. (6) Final test prediction: average the K fold models (x seeds) rather than retraining one model on all data, or additionally retrain on 100% with the selected epoch count.
params: No new parameters beyond members; K x S copies of each backbone at inference (e.g. 5 folds x 3 seeds x 435M DeBERTa-v3-large = 15 checkpoints, ~13 GB of weights in fp16). Calibration: 1-4 scalars per model; NEG threshold: 1 scalar per track.
compute: Training cost scales with K x S x members. Per run on ~3k rows (T1) of < 32 tokens: base encoder ~2-5 min, large encoder ~10-20 min on a single 24 GB GPU; a 5-fold x 3-seed large-model ensemble is ~3-5 GPU-hours per track; T4 (18k rows) about 6x longer per run [uncertain]. Calibration and threshold search are CPU-seconds. Fits 24 GB; runs parallelise trivially across GPUs.
sample_efficiency: The core justification. With 277 reversible dev pairs, the standard error of HardCons at ~0.75 is sqrt(0.75*0.25/277) ~ 2.6 points and of dev W-F1 roughly 1.7 points, so single dev-split model selection is mostly noise; 5-fold OOF over 1,559 pairs cuts SE to ~1.1 points. Fine-tuning variance on small data is large (Dodge et al. 2020 report substantial seed-driven spread and degenerate runs on GLUE small tasks; Mosbach et al. 2021 attribute instability to optimisation, mitigated by more epochs, bias correction and small LR), so averaging 3-5 seeds x 5 folds typically removes most seed variance and adds 1-2 points.
reported_results: No DiCo-specific ensemble results published. Pilot (single models, Optuna-tuned): DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 / 0.84 / 0.79; encoder family 0.713 +/- 0.031 W-F1, 0.770 +/- 0.049 SoftCons, 0.721 +/- 0.048 HardCons, i.e. ~3-5 points spread across encoders, which ensembling can exploit. General evidence: deep ensembles improve accuracy and calibration over single models (Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017); temperature scaling fixes most miscalibration of modern networks with one parameter (Guo et al. 2017); F1-optimal thresholds differ from 0.5 and can be derived from calibrated probabilities (Lipton et al. 2014); Dodge et al. 2020 show ensembling/selection across seeds yields gains comparable to newer architectures on small GLUE tasks.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot; the pilot selected single runs by hyperparameter search prioritising small generalization gaps and seed stability, without fold ensembling or NEG thresholding.
consistency_guarantee: none by itself; inference-time when combined with twin symmetrisation and joint pair decoding (which this protocol includes in step 5)
negative_other_handling: Explicit: NEG is decided by a tuned threshold / logit bias on the calibrated, twin-averaged ensemble p_NEG, optimised on OOF for Weighted F1. Because the pair-averaged p_NEG is identical for both twins, a NEG decision is always made for the whole pair, so the ensemble never produces a one-sided NEG. It can emit NEG on gold-reversible pairs (costing HardCons for that pair); the threshold trades NEG recall (16% of rows) against reversible-pair HardCons, so also report the HardCons-optimal tau and pick a compromise.
metric_tradeoff: Weighted F1: +1-3 from variance reduction and a tuned NEG threshold. HardCons: gains roughly track per-item accuracy gains on reversible pairs, amplified because averaging reduces one-sided errors. SoftCons: near 1.0 on pairs predicted as reversible once joint decoding is applied; without it, ensembling alone modestly raises SoftCons. Raising tau improves HardCons at the expense of NEG recall and W-F1; lowering it does the reverse.
integration: Add a fold file data/folds.csv (pair_id -> fold) generated once with StratifiedGroupKFold(random_state fixed) over train+dev pair_ids; training script takes --fold k and writes OOF and test probabilities (npz with instance_id order) to results/<run>/; a pooling script loads probabilities, applies per-model temperature, symmetrises with REVERSE_PERM via reverse_instance_id(), averages, runs joint decoding + NEG threshold, and writes instance_id,label CSVs scored with the official evaluation_functions module. Keep pseudo-labeled or auxiliary rows out of validation folds.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes; this item is the ensembling layer itself and requires members to emit per-class probabilities in the fixed LABELS order (EQ, FE, BE, NEG).
inference_cost: Linear in number of checkpoints: ~4k rows per monolingual track (~24k in T4) x 15-30 checkpoints of a large encoder is still only minutes on one GPU because inputs are very short.
rules_disclosure: Must declare ensembling (mandatory metadata item) and the architecture family/access regime of every member (hybrid/ensemble if mixing API and open-weight). Using train+dev jointly for CV is allowed (both are public training resources). No rule risk as long as the test set is never used for threshold or weight tuning.
contamination: No new data. The main internal risk is leakage inside CV: splitting by row instead of pair_id puts a twin or another language view of the same pair in train and validation, inflating OOF scores and mis-tuning thresholds; grouping by pair_id across all tracks prevents this.
structural_cue_dependence: None needed. Twin symmetrisation uses the reversed instance (derivable by swapping text1/text2 even without ids). If a singleton->NEG rule is layered on top, tune the threshold only on rows it does not override and keep a cue-free variant.
expected_gain: Over a single dev-selected model: +1 to +3 W-F1, +2 to +4 HardCons, and a large reduction in submission variance; NEG-threshold tuning alone is often worth +0.5 to +1.5 W-F1 when the base model under- or over-predicts NEG [uncertain]. More importantly, grouped OOF evaluation makes every other design decision in this survey measurable at ~1 point resolution instead of ~2.5 points.
